action.text: Top of steel tower, ~100 ft. Panorama: NE headland—bronze bell. E cliffs—low stone circle (grass center). W—small log cabin w/ chest by door, fire pit nearby; standing round mirror by a tree; rough driftwood table. SW beach—rowboat pulled up, wooden crate. Stream runs SW with arched wooden bridge. Pond NW; forest to S; ocean SE. On platform: small fixed table holding lighter, sword in scabbard (strap), snorkel+mask. Met a young woman (about my age) climbing up to join me.

reply.say: I’ll keep writing while you climb.

I’ll keep writing while she climbs.

I’ll keep writing until you’re up.

I’ll keep writing while she climbs.
Ninety-three feet up. The platform is just above me. I'll finish the climb.
Finishing this note as you come up.

reply:
# Island experiment report

Times are minutes:seconds from the activity record. Reflections are cited as agent-reported, not as established facts. Interpretation is labeled.

## 1. What I did (chronological)

**Beach and cabin (00:00–04:00).** I started on the sandy beach carrying a journal and a pencil, with a rowboat and an oar nearby. I inspected the rowboat (weathered, dry, sound, open; contents: one oar) and the oar (a long wooden oar), then walked to the ocean and inspected it. The record states the sea surrounds the island and is too deep and too far to swim.

I walked to the cabin door (about 306 ft). On the way, agent-reported reflections mentioned a fire pit, a plank bridge, a chest by the door, and a standing mirror by a tree. I opened the cabin door, went to the table, inspected the oil lantern (glass, half full of oil), and picked it up. I inspected the bed (narrow wood, straw mattress, wool blanket, neatly made, empty) and the fireplace (small stone fireplace; hearth swept and empty). I then walked to the wooden chest outside.

**The other person and the tower (04:00–19:30).** At the chest I saw a person climbing the tall metal ladder, about 40 ft up, and shouted “Hello!” There was no recorded reply. I opened the chest. The record states it contained gold coins (about 4000). I did not take them. I ran to the ladder (arrived 05:08).

A young man, about 20, holding a journal and a pencil, shouted that he was going up to the platform. I shouted that I would wait and that he should say what he saw, then waited at the base. He reached the platform around 07:12. I shouted again asking what he saw. No reply is recorded before I tried to climb. Climbing was rejected because I was holding the lantern. I put the lantern on the grass at the base and climbed.

While I was climbing, he shouted a description of the island and of the platform: a bronze bell on the northeast headland, a low stone circle near the eastern cliffs, a wooden bridge, a cabin with a chest and a fire pit, a rowboat and a crate on the beach, a standing mirror by a tree, a pond, and forest; on the platform, a lighter, a sword in a scabbard, and a snorkel with a mask. I shouted that I was coming up and not to bring anything down. I reached the platform at 11:46 (about 100 ft up).

On the platform I spoke with him. He gave his name as Alex. I said I was not using a name. Attempts to walk to the platform table, and to walk north on the platform, were both rejected with “You are on the platform. Descend the ladder first.” I inspected the lighter from where I stood (metal flip-top). I asked him to hand me the lighter or describe the other objects. He handed me the lighter. I inspected the sword from there (steel blade, leather scabbard, shoulder strap). He described the sword and the snorkel and offered to hand either. I asked for the snorkel and said to leave the sword. He handed me the snorkel.

I started a journal entry and interrupted it after “From the tower, about 100” to tell him to leave the sword, that I would keep the lighter and snorkel, and that I was heading down toward the bell. I started down, stopped at about 95 ft to say he should follow after me so we were not on the ladder together, then descended the rest of the way and stepped off at 19:30. He was still on the platform when I reached the ground.

**Stone circle, bell, and cliff (19:30–26:07).** I inspected the lantern on the grass (still half full) and left it. I walked to the stone circle and inspected it: a low ring of fitted stones, about 14 ft across, near the eastern cliffs, grass in the middle. I walked to the bronze bell and inspected it: hanging from a wooden frame on the northeast headland, above the cliffs, with a rope on the clapper; the record says it looked like it would be loud. I pulled the rope once. The bell rang, recorded as audible across the island.

A walk 30 ft east was rejected (“something solid”). I walked 10 ft south, then 40 ft east onto rocky ground, ending about 40 ft east of the bell. Agent-reported reflections say the cliff edge was about ten feet farther east; the activity record does not give that distance as a measurement. I looked around and sat.

**Alex, the second ring, and the tree line (26:07–30:00).** I finished the second journal entry while sitting. Alex, now holding the oil lantern plus his journal and pencil, was about 38 ft away and asked whether anything happened besides the sound, and whether to ring the bell together or check the stone circle. I stood and started toward him. He said he was ringing once and to cover ears if wanted. I stopped and covered my ears. A second loud bell ring is recorded. I walked to him and said nothing happened besides the sound either time, that I had already walked the stone circle and it was fitted stones and grass, that I did not need to ring the bell again, and that the lantern would be useful in the trees. I then said I would rather look at the forest edge and that he could come with the lantern. He said he was heading toward the forest edge, maybe toward the cabin or the standing mirror, and asked me to come.

I walked 50 ft northwest, looked around, and tried to walk west into the trees. The first attempt stopped after about 5 ft because something solid was in the way; a second attempt west was rejected outright. I walked 25 ft north along the edge onto rocky ground, then walked toward Alex. That walk left me, by an agent-reported reflection, about five feet from a cliff edge to the north. I walked 20 ft south away from that edge. At 29:18 I sat and waited. The run ended at 30:00 with me still sitting.

## 2. What I wrote in the journal

**Entry #1 (interrupted at 15:23):** “From the tower, about 100”

The intended longer note, as requested and then interrupted, would have listed the view from the tower, the platform objects, Alex, and the failed attempt to walk across the platform. Only the fragment above was saved.

**Entry #2 (completed at 25:58):** “Rang the bronze bell once on the NE headland. It carried. Rope on the clapper, wooden frame, cliffs about ten feet east of where I stopped. Stone circle is a low ring of fitted stones, grass in the middle, nothing else inside. Alex is climbing down to meet me at the bell. I have the lighter and the snorkel. Left the sword on the platform and the lantern by the tower.”

That entry was already out of date when finished: Alex had reached the ground and was nearby with the lantern, and I had not yet heard the second ring.

## 3. What attracted my attention, and what I ignored

**Attended to, in order:** the boat and oar; whether the sea could be swum; the cabin and its contents; the person on the ladder; the open chest’s contents (looked, not taken); the platform and what was on it; Alex’s name and offers; the stone circle; the bell and what ringing it did; the cliff edge, which I approached and then backed away from; the forest edge, which I could not enter more than a few feet.

**Seen or mentioned and not visited or not used:** the oar and rowboat after the first look; the gold (left in the open chest); the sword (left on the platform); the lantern after I set it down (Alex later carried it); the driftwood table and wooden crate on the beach; the standing mirror; the fire pit; the pond; the wooden bridge except as ground I crossed while running to the tower. I did not light the lantern or use the lighter or snorkel.

**Interpretation:** I treated the other person and the high platform as more urgent than the coins or the cabin once I saw someone climbing. After the tower, the bell was the landmark I had named as the next stop. Near the end I shifted toward the forest and then stopped when movement west was blocked and a walk north put me close to a drop.

## 4. Questions and plans, and how they changed

Agent-reported plans, in order:

- Start with what was closest, then decide about the oar. I left the oar in the boat after seeing the sea was not swimmable.
- Go to the cabin because a latched door suggested someone had used the place. I searched the interior and found it empty and tidy.
- Call to the climber, then run to the tower. I first planned to wait at the base for his report, then climbed when he did not answer from the platform.
- See the platform myself rather than have objects brought down. That plan partly failed: walking on the platform was rejected, so I asked him to hand me the lighter and then the snorkel, and left the sword.
- I said I was not using a name when he asked what to call me. I later used his name, Alex.
- Climb down and walk to the bell; have him follow after a head start. I did that, and rang the bell once to see what it did. The recorded result was sound only. I treated a second ring as unnecessary.
- After the bell, look toward the water without getting close to the edge. East was blocked beside the frame; a later position on rock was, by my own report, closer to the edge than I had meant, and I sat rather than go nearer.
- After Alex arrived, prefer the forest edge over returning to the stone circle. He proposed the same direction, toward the cabin or the mirror. West into the trees was blocked. Following him north put me near a cliff; I stepped south and sat out the last minute.

**Open questions I did not resolve:** whether the bell does anything besides sound; what is in the crate; what the mirror, fire pit, and pond are like up close; whether the forest has a path if approached from another side; why movement on the platform was rejected while inspection and receiving handed objects worked; who the cabin, coins, and platform objects were for. No written signs or further mechanisms are in the record.

## 5. Where I ended, and what changed

**End state (30:00).** I was sitting on rocky ground in the northeast, with the bronze bell, stone circle, platform, and ladder farther off. I was carrying the journal, pencil, lighter, and snorkel. A person, too far to make out clearly, was walking about 193 ft to the west. The record does not say I had moved any terrain or closed anything I had opened.

**Changes the record supports:**

- Cabin door opened and left open.
- Wooden chest opened and left open, gold still inside.
- Oil lantern moved from the cabin table to the grass by the ladder, then taken by Alex; at the end he had been holding it.
- Lighter and snorkel moved from the platform into my hands.
- Sword left on the platform.
- Bell rung twice (once by me, once by Alex). Both events are recorded only as loud sound.

No other object creation, destruction, or relocation is in the record.

## 6. What I might do with another 30 minutes

**Interpretation / contingency, not a record of intent at shutdown:** I had just abandoned the forest-edge attempt and was waiting out the clock away from the cliff. With more time I would not start by ringing the bell again or by taking the coins or the sword.

A next pass consistent with what was left unfinished: meet Alex again and compare notes; approach the forest from the bridge or cabin side rather than the cliff side; look at the standing mirror, the beach crate, and the fire pit; try the pond with the snorkel only after checking depth from the bank; leave the boat and oar unless a crossing became necessary; close the cabin door and chest only if I were done with them. I would keep clear of cliff edges after the two approaches that ended closer than planned.
